peerMapping.justification: Three-run Kimi K3 consensus selected only the displayed peers: NVDA 32.7% with 3/3 replicate support; AMD 24.0% with 3/3 replicate support; MU 16.7% with 3/3 replicate support; AMZN 11.0% with 3/3 replicate support; GOOGL 9.0% with 2/3 replicate support; MSFT 6.7% with 2/3 replicate support. Individual rationales state each economic relationship.

peers.name: NVIDIA
peers.reason: NVIDIA is the closest available return comparator for the AI data-center semiconductor impulse that drives Marvell. Both are priced off hyperscaler accelerator buildouts, networking attach, and the pace of AI cluster deployment, so an AI capex upside or downside shock should transmit to both through the same end demand even though their products differ.

peers.name: Advanced Micro Devices
peers.reason: AMD is the second core semiconductor peer because its data-center CPU and GPU franchises are tied to the same AI server procurement cycle as Marvell's custom silicon, optical DSP, switch, and storage connectivity exposure. It is not a product substitute, but it shares the dominant accelerator-led semiconductor revenue revision channel.

peers.name: Micron Technology
peers.reason: Micron is a same-end-market semiconductor comparator tied to AI data-center builds through HBM and memory content. It is not a direct Marvell substitute, but the AI server memory cycle is a close complementary exposure to Marvell's data-center networking and custom-silicon demand.

peers.name: Amazon
peers.reason: Amazon represents the hyperscale cloud customer and end-market channel for Marvell: AWS AI capex, custom accelerator deployment, networking upgrades, and storage infrastructure demand are direct demand signals for Marvell's data-center exposure. Amazon's equity has large non-chip drivers, so it receives a smaller weight than the semiconductor peers.

peers.name: Alphabet
peers.reason: Major hyperscale customer of custom AI silicon; Google's in-house accelerator program is a direct end-market driver of Marvell's custom ASIC revenue.

peers.name: Microsoft
peers.reason: Microsoft is another hyperscale AI capex buyer whose data-center accelerator, Ethernet networking, optical interconnect, and storage buildouts feed the same demand pool Marvell sells into. Like Amazon, its diversified software and cloud revenue dilutes the semiconductor signal, so it anchors the customer side of the basket at the smallest weight.

primary_index_hedge.name: Nasdaq-100
primary_index_hedge.reason: Marvell is a Nasdaq-listed large-cap semiconductor and AI data-center infrastructure name, so the Nasdaq-100 is the cleanest primary hedge for generic systematic, growth-duration, and large-cap technology risk. Its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity of 112.11 USD millions is an execution advantage, not evidence of economic similarity.

peerMapping.historyMethod: daily-rebalanced peer spot total returns using the fixed Kimi weights; the basket begins with the first available selected peer, unavailable pre-listing peers are omitted, and remaining weights are renormalized; the browser rebases the basket to the target spot level at the first shared date of each selected chart range

liveSplice.method: current Hyperliquid native or TradeXYZ perp mid divided by that peer's matching-venue perp close on its latest spot date; available Kimi weights are renormalized and applied as a one-period return from the published peer spot endpoint; USD cash close is retained for disclosure but never mixed with a differently scaled perp contract

earningsOptions.source: Schwab listed-options chain, FMP earnings calendars, and Sharadar adjusted prices

liquidityFilter.sides: OTM puts below spot and OTM calls above spot

model.name: liquid vertical-spread risk-neutral CDF
model.description: Liquid vertical spreads are used when the chain supplies at least four valid probability points; otherwise the nearest liquid ATM straddle supplies the expiration distribution. Earnings-date log distances are time-scaled from the first post-event expiration.
model.measure: risk-neutral, not a historical or physical forecast

historicalAnalysis.eventSource: SEC earnings release history with FMP historical calendar fallback
historicalAnalysis.method: Each current two-leg structure is translated into percentage-of-spot strikes and debit. Those same normalized strikes and today's debit percentage are replayed across prior earnings using the same calendar-day entry lead and post-event exit horizon. A profitable event requires expiration payoff greater than the original debit.
historicalAnalysis.limitation: Stock-path proxy using today's premium; historical option quotes, bid-ask execution, volatility repricing, early exercise, dividends, and transaction costs are not reconstructed.
